subject: Literacy
title: Sounds around us
objectives: Children will stop, listen and say or show what they hear.
Children will match a sound to the thing that makes it with support.
content: Stopping to listen, finding the sources of everyday sounds inside and outside, and guessing hidden sounds.
teachingActivities: Model listening with a finger to your ear and a calm face; whisper the instruction "Shh, listen"; name each sound clearly and give children time to point.
learnerActivities: Stop, listen, point to or name what they hear, and join a guess-the-sound game.
resources: A bell, a spoon and a cup, a rattle
A cloth bag
Pictures of a door, a bird, a car and a tap
A small drum
assessment: Observe whether each child stops to listen, turns towards a sound and points to its source.
expectedOutcomes: Stays still to listen for a short time.
Names or points to the source of a familiar sound.
crossCurricular: Physical Development: walking in a line

lessons.title: Shh, listen!
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will stop and stay still to listen for a few seconds.
successCriteria: Stops moving when the teacher says "Shh, listen"
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they may respond to their name, turn towards sounds and enjoy simple songs.
resources: A small bell
A cloth to cover the bell
A carpet or mat for sitting
lessons.starter: Sit the children in a circle, put a finger to your ear and whisper "Shh, listen." Ring the bell once and let the sound fade.
teacherActivities: Whisper "Shh, listen" and ring the bell once. Hold still until the sound fades, then say "I heard a bell."
Ring the bell behind your back. Ask "What can you hear?" and wait a few seconds.
Teach the listening action: finger to the ear, then say "listen" together.
Ring the bell again and let each child ring it once while the others listen.
learnerActivities: Children stop, look at you and listen.
Children turn towards the sound or say or point to the bell.
Children copy the action and say "listen".
Each child rings gently and the others stay still to listen.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Whisper "Shh, listen" and ring the bell once. Hold still until the sound fades, then say "I heard a bell." Children: Children stop, look at you and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Ring the bell behind your back. Ask "What can you hear?" and wait a few seconds. Children: Children turn towards the sound or say or point to the bell.
Step 3. Teacher: Teach the listening action: finger to the ear, then say "listen" together. Children: Children copy the action and say "listen".
Step 4. Teacher: Ring the bell again and let each child ring it once while the others listen. Children: Each child rings gently and the others stay still to listen.

practical.title: Listening statues
steps: Ask children to walk gently round the mat while you hum.
Ring the bell and say "Shh, listen". Everyone stands still like a statue.
When the sound fades, children wave and walk again. Repeat four times.
practical.safety: Clear the mat of toys and chairs so children can move safely. Keep the bell sound gentle so it does not startle anyone.

differentiation.support: Sit the child on your lap and put a hand on theirs to show the listening action.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to ring the bell for the group and tell friends to listen.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you listen?
questions.expected: Child stops and looks or points to the ear.

questions.question: What did you hear?
questions.expected: Bell, or a pointing gesture towards it.

expectedOutcomes: Stops to listen for a few seconds
lessons.conclusion: Whisper "Shh, listen" one last time and finish with a quiet clap. Say "Good listening."
lessons.homeConnection: At home, say "Shh, listen" and ask your child to point to the sound they hear, such as a fan or a car.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "stop and stay still to listen for a few seconds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A child with a finger to the ear
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Listen, listen, shh, shh, shh. What can you hear? What can you hear?

lessons.title: Inside sounds
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will point to the objects that make sounds in the classroom.
successCriteria: Points to an object that makes a sound
Copies a sound with the voice
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they may respond to their name, turn towards sounds and enjoy simple songs.
resources: A spoon and a cup
A rattle
A door that can be closed
A tap or water jug
lessons.starter: Tap a spoon on a cup and say "Tap, tap, tap. What is making the sound?" Let children point to the spoon.
teacherActivities: Make three sounds in turn: tap the cup, shake the rattle, close the door. Name each one.
Make a sound with your back turned and ask "What was that?"
Pour water from the jug into a basin. Say "Splash, splash."
Give each child one object to make a sound while the others listen.
learnerActivities: Children watch and point to each thing that made the sound.
Children point to the object or say the word.
Children listen and say "splash".
Child makes a sound; friends point to what they heard.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Make three sounds in turn: tap the cup, shake the rattle, close the door. Name each one. Children: Children watch and point to each thing that made the sound.
Step 2. Teacher: Make a sound with your back turned and ask "What was that?" Children: Children point to the object or say the word.
Step 3. Teacher: Pour water from the jug into a basin. Say "Splash, splash." Children: Children listen and say "splash".
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child one object to make a sound while the others listen. Children: Child makes a sound; friends point to what they heard.

practical.title: Sound basket
steps: Put four safe sound-makers in a basket.
Each child takes one out and makes its sound.
Everyone says the name of the object together.
practical.safety: Use only large, smooth objects that cannot be swallowed. Keep the rattle sound soft and watch that children do not put objects in their mouths.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects only and let the child choose which to shake.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose an object and make a sound for friends to name.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What makes this sound?
questions.expected: Child names or points to the object.

expectedOutcomes: Points to the source of a classroom sound
Makes a sound with an object
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects back in the basket one at a time, saying each name together.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to find something at home that makes a sound, such as a spoon on a pot.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "point to the objects that make sounds in the classroom" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Outside sounds
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will listen outside and say or point to what they hear.
successCriteria: Points to or names a sound heard outside
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they may respond to their name, turn towards sounds and enjoy simple songs.
resources: Pictures of a bird, a car, a hen and the wind
A safe outdoor area
A hat for each child where needed
lessons.starter: Show the picture of a bird and say "Tweet, tweet. We will listen for a bird outside." Hold a finger to your ear.
teacherActivities: Walk the children in a line to the safe outdoor area, holding the rope or hands.
Stop, say "Shh, listen" and wait ten seconds. Say what you hear, such as a bird.
Show the four pictures. Ask "Did we hear a bird? A car?"
Walk to a second spot and listen again.
learnerActivities: Children walk gently and hold their place in the line.
Children stop and listen, and some point or name a sound.
Children point to the picture of the sound they heard.
Children listen and say "car", "bird" or make the sound.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk the children in a line to the safe outdoor area, holding the rope or hands. Children: Children walk gently and hold their place in the line.
Step 2. Teacher: Stop, say "Shh, listen" and wait ten seconds. Say what you hear, such as a bird. Children: Children stop and listen, and some point or name a sound.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the four pictures. Ask "Did we hear a bird? A car?" Children: Children point to the picture of the sound they heard.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk to a second spot and listen again. Children: Children listen and say "car", "bird" or make the sound.

practical.title: Listening spots
steps: Choose two spots outside, such as the gate and the tree.
At each spot, listen for ten seconds.
Point to the matching picture card.
practical.safety: Keep children in a line with an adult at the front and back, away from the road and the gate. Check the ground for sharp objects and use sun hats in strong sun.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and point to the thing that makes the sound.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend one sound they heard.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What can you hear?
questions.expected: Bird, car, wind or a sound made with the voice.

questions.question: Is it loud or quiet?
questions.expected: Child answers loud or quiet by word or gesture.

expectedOutcomes: Names or imitates one outside sound
lessons.conclusion: Walk back in a line and say "We listened well outside."
lessons.homeConnection: On the way home or at the compound, ask "What can you hear?" and wait for your child to point.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "listen outside and say or point to what they hear" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Tweet, tweet, tweet, I hear a bird. Brum, brum, brum, I hear a car.

lessons.title: Guess the sound
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will match a hidden sound to a picture of its source.
successCriteria: Points to the picture that matches a sound
Waits quietly while the sound is made
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they may respond to their name, turn towards sounds and enjoy simple songs.
resources: A cloth bag
A bell, a rattle and a spoon with a cup
Three picture cards of the same objects
lessons.starter: Show the cloth bag and say "I have a secret sound in my bag. Shh, listen." Shake it softly.
teacherActivities: Put the bell in the bag, shake it and ask "What is it?" Take it out to show.
Lay the three picture cards on the mat. Make a sound behind a screen.
Repeat with the rattle and the spoon and cup.
Let a child choose a card and ask you to make that sound.
learnerActivities: Children listen, guess by pointing or naming, and look at the reveal.
Children point to the matching picture.
Children point and say the object name.
Child points to a card and listens to the sound.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the bell in the bag, shake it and ask "What is it?" Take it out to show. Children: Children listen, guess by pointing or naming, and look at the reveal.
Step 2. Teacher: Lay the three picture cards on the mat. Make a sound behind a screen. Children: Children point to the matching picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Repeat with the rattle and the spoon and cup. Children: Children point and say the object name.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child choose a card and ask you to make that sound. Children: Child points to a card and listens to the sound.

practical.title: Sound lotto
steps: Place three picture cards on the mat.
Hide behind a screen and make one sound.
Children point to the matching card, and the teacher shows the object.
practical.safety: Use soft sounds only so no child is frightened. Keep objects large and out of mouths.

differentiation.support: Offer two cards instead of three and make the sound twice.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to hide behind the screen and make a sound for the group.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is the sound?
questions.expected: Child names or points to the matching picture.

questions.question: Is it the bell?
questions.expected: Yes or no with a nod or word.

expectedOutcomes: Matches a sound to its picture with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say "Shh, listen" for a last quiet moment.
lessons.homeConnection: Play guess the sound at home with a spoon and a pot and ask your child to point to what made it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match a hidden sound to a picture of its source" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 listening check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child listens and responds to sounds.
successCriteria: Points to or names the source of one sound
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children are new to the class; they may respond to their name, turn towards sounds and enjoy simple songs.
resources: A bell, a rattle, a spoon and cup
Three picture cards
Class record sheet
lessons.starter: Sing "Listen, listen, shh, shh, shh" and show the three listening stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations and rotate groups every four minutes. Station 1: bell and rattle. Station 2: picture cards. Station 3: listening statues.
Make one sound at each station and ask "What can you hear?"
Record each child’s level and take a photograph for the portfolio.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station and stop to listen on the signal.
Child points to or names the source.
Children play on and tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations and rotate groups every four minutes. Station 1: bell and rattle. Station 2: picture cards. Station 3: listening statues. Children: Children play at each station and stop to listen on the signal.
Step 2. Teacher: Make one sound at each station and ask "What can you hear?" Children: Child points to or names the source.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take a photograph for the portfolio. Children: Children play on and tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Listening stations
steps: Set up three stations with soft sound-makers.
practical.safety: Use soft, large objects only and supervise every station. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one familiar sound.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to ring the bell for friends to listen.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: stops to listen; turns towards a sound; points to or names a sound source.

questions.question: What made that sound?
questions.expected: Child names or points to the object.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
Listens to a sound for a few seconds
lessons.conclusion: Whisper "Good listening" and wave goodbye to the sound-makers.
lessons.homeConnection: Say "Shh, listen" at home and ask your child to point to the sound.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child listens and responds to sounds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
